core_obligations: Reduction to the quotients (proof lines 2628-2640): let F be the property (I) filtration on I; the short exact sequence of lemma-property-I-sequence produces a distinguished triangle, and by derived-lemma-representable-homological it suffices to show Hom_K(N, I/F_i I) = 0 for all acyclic N and all i.

Reduction to the graded pieces (proof lines 2641-2648): each quotient I/F_i I has a finite filtration by admissible monomorphisms whose graded pieces are products of shifts of A-dual, so it suffices to treat a single product of A-dual[k].
The terminal case (proof lines 2649-2652): Hom_K(N, A-dual[k]) = 0 for acyclic N by lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free together with the exactness of the duality functor.
proof_roadmap: Convert the property (I) filtration into a distinguished triangle and reduce to the quotients.
Reduce each quotient through its finite admissible filtration to products of shifted duals.
Conclude by the explicit computation of Hom into shifts of the dual and exactness of the dual.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the K-injectivity of property (I) modules: no acyclic module maps to them in the homotopy category (statement lines 2620-2627). The proof (lines 2629-2652) is a complete reduction chain in the span: the filtration triangle with the representable-homological reduction, the finite admissible filtration of the quotients down to products of shifts of the dual, and the terminal computation through the Hom-into-shift-dual lemma and exactness of the dual. H2: the two-step reduction architecture carries the proof and each reduction is verifiable in the span; the lemma underwrites every property-(I) computation in the chapter.
